title: Instant Photo Book Platform Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Photo book and photo product providers that compete for the same consumers and jobs as PastBook, the Amsterdam '1-click photo book' platform modeled in this domain: a family memory keeper, traveller, Facebook archivist or seasonal gift giver who wants thousands of phone or Facebook photos turned into a printed hardcover book, calendar or poster without designing anything, paid per order, produced by a partner printer in or near the customer's country and delivered within days to one of 150+ countries. PastBook is included as the modeled company so that the other players' scale (CEWE's 6.32 million photobook copies, Mixbook's 6 million customers, Popsa's 2 million customers) can be read against its own 10 million+ books since 2012, 1 million+ app downloads and USD 14.3M of 2019 revenue.
inclusionLogic: European photofinishing incumbents with their own factories and multi-brand portfolios (CEWE, Storio group, smartphoto group) that sell photobooks to the same European households, mostly through an editor-led design flow and a large in-house production footprint that PastBook deliberately does not own

US mass-market photo product incumbents (Shutterfly, Snapfish) that dominate the North American market where about 80 percent of PastBook's customers live and that compete on catalogue breadth, constant promotions and low entry prices

mobile-first and AI-assisted challengers (Mixbook Studio, Chatbooks subscription Monthbooks, Popsa) whose automated design, phone import and repeat-order mechanics attack the same 'a book in minutes, no design effort' promise that is PastBook's core differentiator

big-tech photo libraries with a built-in print store (Google Photos) that already hold the customer's photos, surface on-device 'memories' and can sell a book without any import step, the platform substitute PastBook must stay ahead of on curation quality

premium quality specialists (Saal Digital) that win the traveller and milestone celebrant who cares about print quality above speed, an adjacent segment that sets the quality bar PastBook's partner printers are measured against
notes: Business stats are only included when they come from official company pages, investor releases or the company's own press releases as listed in the domain's ID spine; each stat preserves the reported period and scope. Where only third-party estimates exist (Shutterfly revenue, Popsa revenue, smartphoto group revenue) they are omitted or mentioned in the description as unverified, never recorded as an official stat.

Players report at very different scopes: CEWE reports IFRS group turnover and photobook copies for a listed group with about 4,000 employees, Storio group and Mixbook publish cumulative customer or project counters, Popsa publishes revenue per employee and headcount in a blog post, Saal Digital and PastBook cite review scores, and Google publishes only product specifications. None of these figures are directly comparable with each other or with PastBook's 10 million+ books created since 2012.

PastBook figures mix official company pages (books created, downloads, prices), the investor page of Vortex Capital Partners, funding and award press releases (2015, 2017, 2019) and a 2021 press article for the 2019 revenue and 2020 projection; the 2020 revenue figure is a projection quoted at the time, not an audited result.

Prices are quoted as published on the respective official pages at the time of access, in the currency shown, before promotions; most players run continuous discounts, so list prices overstate the price actually paid.

Several players belong to larger groups: Snapfish is owned by District Photo, Shutterfly by Apollo Global Management since 2019, Storio group is the former albelli-Photobox Group (rebranded March 2024) and Google Photos is a Google product; PastBook's own CEO and CMO previously worked at Albelli, one of the Storio brands.
Region vocabulary follows the repository convention (europe, north_america, asia_pacific, global); category vocabulary is incumbent, challenger, big-tech, adjacent and modeled-company.

players.name: PastBook (modeled company)
players.description: PastBook is the modeled subject of this domain: an Amsterdam '1-click photo book' platform founded in 2012 in the Rockstart Accelerator by Stefano Cutello with the mission to make reliving memories frictionless, and backed by Vortex Capital Partners since a EUR 350k seed round in December 2015 and a USD 2M convertible note in September 2017. Instead of an editor, the iOS and Android app or the website imports photos from the phone camera roll (by date, location, album or Yearbook mode), from Facebook (one book per year from 2009 to 2025) or from a computer, Dropbox or Google Drive, and a patent-pending curation engine scores image quality, removes duplicates and blurry shots, groups moments and lays out a hardcover book with cover, theme colours and captions in under 60 seconds, ready for a free preview. Customers pay per product with no subscription: a Small Hardcover 8.5 x 6 inch book starts at USD 19.99 for 24 pages plus USD 0.40 per extra page, a Large Hardcover 12 x 8.5 inch book at USD 34.99 plus USD 0.55 per page, wall calendars at USD 24.99 and 34.99 and posters at USD 29.99 and 39.99, in seven currencies and ten languages. Print-ready files are routed to partner printing facilities on four continents that produce most orders in the customer's country on FSC-certified paper and ship to 150+ countries within published windows of 3 to 10 business days. The company reports 10 million+ books created since 2012, 1 million+ app downloads and a Trustpilot TrustScore of 4.5 from 35,837 reviews with every negative review answered within 48 hours by a 24/7 support team in the Netherlands, the United States, Sri Lanka and India. Revenue reached USD 14.3M in 2019 and was projected to triple to about USD 42.9M in 2020, which earned Deloitte Technology Fast50 podium places in 2019 (4,623 percent growth) and 2021 and three consecutive FT1000 listings; since April 2020 the company is led by CEO Wouter Staatsen, formerly CEO of Albelli and VP at Cimpress. It is listed here so that the incumbents' factory-led scale and the challengers' AI and subscription mechanics can be read against PastBook's asset-light, curation-first, per-order model.

players.name: CEWE
players.description: CEWE (cewe.de, company.cewe.de) is Europe's photobook market leader: a listed photofinishing group from Oldenburg with about 4,000 employees in 21 countries that sold a record 6.32 million CEWE PHOTOBOOK copies in 2025 and more than 100 million since the product launched, on group turnover of EUR 864.5M and EBIT of EUR 88.2M. Its model is the opposite of PastBook's: an editor-led design experience in downloadable software, web and app, produced in its own European plants and sold through retail partners as well as online, with the Q4 Christmas peak driving the year. For a European family or gift giver CEWE is the default brand and price anchor; PastBook competes against it with one-click AI curation, no software to learn and delivery in 3 to 5 business days in Germany, France, the Netherlands and Italy from partner printers rather than owned factories. CEWE's 2026 guidance of EUR 870-900M turnover shows the scale gap between the incumbent and a scale-up with USD 14.3M of 2019 revenue.

players.name: Storio group (albelli, Photobox, bonusprint, Posterxxl, Fotoknudsen, Hofmann, Önskefoto)
players.description: Storio group (storiogroup.com), the former albelli-Photobox Group rebranded in March 2024 and led by CEO Alessandro Coppo, is PastBook's Amsterdam neighbour and Europe's second photobook heavyweight: six brands in thirteen European markets, over eleven million customers, multiple manufacturing sites across Europe and consolidated revenue above EUR 340M. Its brands (albelli in the Benelux, Photobox and bonusprint in the UK and France, Posterxxl in Germany, Fotoknudsen and Önskefoto in the Nordics, Hofmann in Spain) sell editor-designed photobooks, prints and wall art from owned factories with heavy promotional pricing. The group is the most direct comparison for PastBook's European ambitions and its former talent pool: PastBook's CEO Wouter Staatsen and CMO Daniel Scheijen both came from Albelli. Where Storio owns production and brands per country, PastBook runs one global brand, one app and a partner-print network, and wins on the speed from photo library to finished book.

players.name: Shutterfly
players.description: Shutterfly (shutterfly.com), founded in 1999 and owned by Apollo Global Management since 2019, is the largest US personalised photo products brand and the incumbent in the North American market that provides about 80 percent of PastBook's customers. It sells photo books alongside cards, prints, gifts and home decor from its own US production, through a template-driven editor, an app and near-constant promotions and free-print programmes. Against Shutterfly's catalogue breadth and brand recognition PastBook positions the opposite promise: no design work, a book generated from the camera roll in under a minute, and a simple two-size hardcover price list. No official business statistic could be verified within this domain's research scope; third-party e-commerce revenue estimates exist but are not recorded here.

players.name: Snapfish
players.description: Snapfish (snapfish.com), owned by District Photo, is the value end of the US photo book market and ships to the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, France, Italy, Australia and New Zealand, an overlap with PastBook's largest markets in North America, Australia and the UK. Its range runs from 5 x 7 to 12 x 12 inch books in hardcover, softcover, layflat, linen and leather, with an 8 x 11 inch hardcover from USD 13.50, well under PastBook's USD 19.99 small hardcover entry price. Snapfish competes on price and format choice through a classic upload-and-design flow; PastBook answers with automated curation and layout, fewer but curated formats and local partner production in the destination country. For the seasonal gift giver the two are compared on the same axes: price after discounts, delivery before the date and print quality.

players.name: Mixbook
players.description: Mixbook (mixbook.com), founded in 2006 in Redwood City, is the design-quality challenger in the US photo book market with 6 million+ customers and 20 million+ projects printed, books of up to 400 pages, an iOS app and shipping to Australia, Canada, the EU and the UK. Its Mixbook Studio AI design tool and Story Mode automate layout and storytelling for customers who still want to edit, which puts it on a collision course with PastBook's curation-first approach from the editor side. Mixbook markets itself as '#1 rated in photo books' and wins the traveller and milestone celebrant who values design control and premium finishes; PastBook wins the same customer when speed and zero effort matter more than control. Both are per-order businesses with no subscription, so the contest is over conversion from free preview to paid book and over print quality per dollar.

players.name: Chatbooks
players.description: Chatbooks (chatbooks.com), founded in 2014 in Lehi, Utah by Nate and Vanessa Quigley, pioneered the subscription photo book: Monthbooks are automatically assembled and printed from the phone camera roll or Instagram feed each month, so the family memory keeper never has to start a project. It raised a USD 11.5M Series B in 2017 and is the clearest alternative business model to PastBook's pay-per-book approach, trading a lower price per small softcover for recurring revenue and habit. PastBook competes for the same US parents with a one-off hardcover yearbook curated by AI from a whole year of photos, yearbook reminders instead of a subscription, and larger premium formats. Chatbooks' Instagram-native origins also mirror the source risk PastBook lived through when Instagram withdrew third-party access.

players.name: Popsa
players.description: Popsa (popsa.com) is the closest like-for-like rival to PastBook: a London mobile-first photo book app that auto-designs books from phone photos, serves 2 million customers in 50+ countries with marketing in 12 languages, and reports USD 1M of revenue per employee with a team of 46 people. It applies AI not only to book design but across marketing, customer support, supplier negotiation and logistics, and like PastBook outsources printing to partners rather than owning factories. The two compete head-on for the family memory keeper and traveller on curation quality, app conversion and print partner reach, with Popsa strongest in the UK and Europe and PastBook strongest in North America and Australia. A third-party 2025 revenue estimate circulates in trade press but is not recorded here as an official figure.

players.name: Google Photos photo books
players.description: Google Photos (photos.google.com) sells photo books directly from the library where billions of consumers already keep their pictures: a 7-inch softcover and a 9-inch hardcover of 20 to 140 pages, printed in 2 to 4 business days and delivered in the United States, Canada and 28+ European countries, with US economy shipping in 8 to 11 business days. Because the photos, the on-device 'memories' and the face and place grouping are already there, Google removes the import step that PastBook's phone and Facebook connectors exist to solve, which makes it the most important platform substitute in this landscape. PastBook's defence is deeper curation and automatic design, more formats (large hardcover, calendars, posters), 150+ destination countries and a brand built only around printed memories, while Google treats books as a small add-on to storage. Google is also a platform PastBook depends on, through Google Play distribution and the Google Drive import, so the relationship is competitor and channel at once.

players.name: Saal Digital
players.description: Saal Digital (saal-digital.com), a family-run German photo lab founded in 1981 with production in Röttenbach, is the premium quality specialist of the field: photo books printed on real photo paper, delivery to more than 25 countries in Europe and the US, a 4.9 out of 5 score from over 235,000 verified reviews and many orders leaving production within 24 hours. It serves photographers and quality-focused consumers who design their book in dedicated software and pay for archival materials, an adjacent segment rather than a one-click audience. For PastBook it defines the print-quality bar the traveller and milestone celebrant compares against and the speed of an owned single-site lab, whereas PastBook relies on partner printers close to the customer. Saal's review volume also shows how strongly verified ratings drive this category, the same lever PastBook works through its Trustpilot and App Store scores.

players.name: smartphoto group (smartphoto, naYan, TopFanZ, Image Insight)
players.description: smartphoto group (smartphotogroup.com) from Wetteren, Belgium is a regional multi-brand photofinisher active in 12 European countries with the smartphoto consumer brand, the naYan personalised gifts brand, TopFanZ fan merchandise and Image Insight, and was delisted from Euronext Brussels on 9 July 2025. Like CEWE and Storio it owns production and sells editor-designed photobooks, calendars and gifts with seasonal promotions, competing for the same Benelux and wider European households that PastBook reaches through its app and Facebook flow. It is the smallest of the European incumbents and illustrates the mid-sized factory-owning model PastBook chose not to build; a third-party 2024 revenue figure exists but is not recorded here as an official stat. Against smartphoto PastBook competes on zero-effort curation, ten-language global reach and local partner production in the destination country.
